assertions.name: A6_both_named_escapes_are_closed_in_the_hull
assertions.source: (b) caps at 1 (qou-m896); (a) cannot lift it at any crossing count (A3); escape needs beta outside [0,1]

description: Runs escape (a) — more than one crossing per bond — named by qou-v3u2 and motivated by qou-m896's finding that the (T,S) grading caps the channel-asymmetry ratio at 1. It fails, and the reason subsumes the question. The Hecke relation T^2 = hT + 1 fixes the eigenvalue product at q.(-1/q) = -1, so a crossing's two block ratios multiply to (q+d)(-1/q+d) = d^2 + dh - 1 = det(T + dI), whose magnitude on d in [-h,0] lies in [1, 1.010926552] — always >= 1, with equality only at the endpoints. A bond built from k crossings multiplies those factors, so |mu_sym . mu_anti| >= 1 for ANY crossing count, hence L(T=0) + L(T=1) <= 0 and the ratio is capped at 1 regardless. Verified on 200 random multi-crossing bonds (k=2..6): det products all >= 1, best ratio 0.927. THE ESCAPE CONDITION is |d^2+dh-1| < 1 <=> 0 < d(d+h) < 2, which fails everywhere in the interior (d(d+h) < 0 there) and holds only for d > 0 (beta < 0) or d < -h (beta > 1): the bond operator must LEAVE THE CONVEX HULL of {sigma, sigma^-1}. No crossing count, block grading or convention does that. Even outside the hull, matching nature's 33.7 requires beta* = -4.30937 (4.31 outside) with |mu_anti| = 5.944e-11, i.e. the T=0 channel tuned to within 6e-11 of unbinding, and the point is not robust (ratio falls to 13.19 at d* - 1e-4). Near-threshold tuning is not itself unphysical — the real NN system is unnatural in exactly that way — but leaving the hull is the structural problem and nothing in the construction supplies it.
caveats: SCOPE: this closes escape (a) for bonds built as a PRODUCT of crossings (T + d_i) with each d_i real and in [-h, 0], which is what the construction uses and what escape (a) proposed. It does NOT close every conceivable multi-crossing construction — a bond that is a SUM of products, or that entangles the two nucleons' internal strands rather than acting on a single interface generator, is not covered by the determinant argument and is not tested here.

THE 'BOUND <=> |mu| < 1' CONVENTION IS INHERITED FROM qou-m896 and is doing real work here too: the antisymmetric block's eigenvalue is negative, so the magnitude is used. Under a convention treating a negative ratio as unphysical the T=0 channel has no binding reading and the whole (T,S) line of argument does not run. The det-magnitude obstruction in A1-A3 is independent of that choice; the ratio numbers in A5 are not.

beta* = -4.309 is a solution of a ONE-PARAMETER family (a single crossing with a free real offset), presented to size what nature would cost, NOT as a proposed value. It has no derivation, sits far outside any braid-crossing reading, and requires a 10-digit tuning. It should be read as a measurement of the gap, not a fit.

The pionless-EFT remark is context, not evidence. The scattering lengths and force range are quoted to establish that near-threshold tuning is a real feature of the NN system; no claim is made that this construction's fine-tuning is the same phenomenon, and the two tunings are not on a common scale.
